1  Model validation

The single-turn analytic core against published runs. prime-rl is the clean anchor: its MFU and E[R] are both pinned by its own published numbers, and it matches to +0%. The rest under-predict. AReaL 14B/32B is the FSDP penalty beyond calibrated MFU, growing with shard degree. INTELLECT-3 is low MoE MFU plus multi-turn context. INTELLECT-2 is broadcast-bound on a weaker volunteer swarm. Whiskers are 90% Monte-Carlo intervals over the unpublished inputs (table A4); validation/REPORT.md reads them.

2  Feasibility

What each RL budget costs a decentralised actor, and which levers move it. A run that misses its window is never dropped: a hollow bar is drawn at the GPUs that reach the fastest achievable wall-clock (the whole stock, split optimally), with that wall-clock written in it. No-fit means the weights or the trainer replica exceed one node. Past a point more GPUs stop helping: each step has a serial floor (the weight broadcast over the WAN, or decode streaming the weights from HBM), so only bigger batches, faster links or more bandwidth per node buy wall-clock.

2.1  Decentralised vs centralised

Decentralisation costs serial latency, from two sources. (i) Weights cross the WAN every step: the trainer's gradient all-reduce between its sites, and the broadcast to inference. (ii) The number of inference waves, set by the HBM a node pools. A datacentre relaxes both: 72-GPU NVL72 nodes on a ~1 Tbps fabric, against 16-GPU islands on 1 Gbps. Everything else is held fixed, so the gap between paired bars is the decentralisation penalty. 2r/2s isolate node size. 2t/2u isolate trainer placement: at Rahman's 150x gradient compression the all-reduce hides under the broadcast; below ~2x the broadcast's compression it binds. An MoE pays both transfers on its total parameters but computes on its active ones, so it sits an order of magnitude lower.

3  Response lengths

E[R] is not one number. In the measurement campaign it moves ~2x along each of three axes, and they multiply: model (same prompts), difficulty, and task (code vs math). The task multiplier is itself family-dependent: V4-pro's code runs 3.4x its math, GLM-4.5-Air's 1.35x, Qwen3's ~1.05x. Within a family, length tracks the post-training recipe, not size: Qwen3 8B/14B are distilled and short, while 32B went through reasoning RL and runs long. Within a run the distribution is heavy-tailed (3e: cv 0.3-1.6, mean above median, p95 ~2-3x the mean). The model carries that spread exactly through E[R^2] = E[R]^2 (1 + cv^2), so cv = 1.6 inflates the attention and KV terms 3.6x. Agentic episodes (3c) are the multi-turn regime the single-turn model does not yet represent. Method and full findings: experiments/RESPONSE_LENGTH_MEASUREMENT.md.

3e  Within-run spread: coefficient of variation of response length

The model takes E[R^2] = E[R]^2 (1 + cv^2), so cv = 1 doubles the attention and KV terms and cv = 1.6 multiplies them 3.6x; the default threat model uses cv = 0.5. Censored runs understate their cv (table 3d).
